standards.title: CUBIC for Fast and Long-Distance Networks

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: Elapsed CUBIC epoch time excludes intervals where application or flow control prevents window updates.
The Reno-friendly region selects W_est when it exceeds the current CUBIC curve value.
Reno-friendly alpha becomes one once W_est reaches the congestion window saved before reduction.
The concave region increments cwnd by the bounded target-minus-window ratio for acknowledged bytes.
The convex region uses the same bounded per-ACK target-minus-window increment rule.
Packet loss immediately reduces the CUBIC congestion window and slow-start threshold on entering recovery.
Every independent CUBIC congestion response uses the recommended multiplicative factor beta of 0.7.
A cwnd-based implementation prevents congestion-window growth when bytes in flight do not fill cwnd.
The QUIC connection path applies the cwnd-based sparse-flight safeguard before every CUBIC ACK update.
Independent ECN congestion events continue reducing CUBIC until one maximum datagram remains.
Persistent CE at one datagram exponentially reduces pacing rate while retaining one complete send opportunity.
Multi-flow mode shortens W_max with the RFC fast-convergence factor after a lower saturation point.
A known single-CUBIC-flow environment should disable the fast-convergence heuristic.
requirements.reason: The pure controller supports and diagnoses an explicit single-flow mode, but the public runtime has no trustworthy topology signal and currently chooses multi-flow fast convergence by default rather than guessing that an Internet path carries only one flow.

requirements.summary: A TCP retransmission timeout resets W_est to the window at the next congestion-avoidance epoch.
requirements.reason: QUIC has probe timeouts but no TCP retransmission-timeout congestion event; RFC 9438 itself states that QUIC loss is detected only after an acknowledgment, so this TCP-only transition is absent.

requirements.summary: A late optional spurious-loss restoration keeps newer state after cwnd has already exceeded its saved value.
requirements.reason: The optional spurious-fast-retransmit restoration algorithm is not implemented, so there is no saved stale CUBIC state that could overwrite a newer window; ordinary late acknowledgments retain current state.

requirements.summary: CUBIC uses a bounded slow-start algorithm whenever cwnd has not exceeded ssthresh.
The initial CUBIC slow start uses the RFC 9406 HyStart++ delay and Conservative Slow Start states.
The CUBIC curve never uses the inefficient low growth constant C equals 0.04.
The fixed-point curve uses the recommended C equals 0.4 coefficient without floating-point drift.

entries.reason: The rejected proposal would redefine cwnd_prior as flight size; the published definition and RFC 9002 safeguards remain authoritative.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: The key configuration a client encapsulates against is authenticated and integrity protected so no other entity can substitute one it can read.
requirements.reason: Authentication here is a property of how the configuration was retrieved, and this package fetches nothing: a caller hands it the bytes it obtained. What the codec can answer, that the bytes decode to exactly one well formed configuration or to none, it answers in decode_key_configuration.

requirements.summary: A key configuration collection with any incorrectly encoded member is discarded whole rather than partly accepted, so recovery differences cannot segregate clients.
Any field the relay's own request carries beside the encapsulated body is independent of that body.
The request the relay forwards to the gateway is built from the fixed gateway URI, the fixed content type, and the body, so nothing an inbound request carried survives into it.
No inbound header, address, connection identifier, or credential enters the value the relay forwards, so the relay adds nothing a client is unaware of.
Anything the relay passes back that came from the gateway is the encapsulated response itself; nothing unencapsulated is carried out of it.
The relay's response to its client carries a 200, a content type, and the encapsulated body, and nothing else.
requirements.reason: The status and fields of the relay's own response are set where that response is composed, and this package composes no HTTP response. forward_response yields the encapsulated body alone and contributes no field to put beside it.

requirements.summary: A client does not build an encapsulated request carrying a 100-continue expectation, because the exchange cannot convey the interim response it asks for.
A gateway handed a request carrying a 100-continue expectation answers with an error instead of forwarding it to the target.
Every refusal is a typed error naming which rule failed, so the resource answering it has a client-error condition to report rather than a silent drop.
An error a gateway detects after decapsulation succeeds is answered inside an encapsulated response, which needs the response context that decapsulation produced.
The hop this package constrains, relay to gateway, is bound to one https URI at construction and refuses any other scheme; the client's own hop is the request it composes, which nothing here builds.
A client has a mechanism to decide that a given gateway may be used for a given target, because it does not authenticate the target itself.
requirements.reason: Deciding that a particular gateway may speak for a particular target is a trust decision made when the deployment is configured, not one a codec can make from the bytes it is given. The gateway side of that pairing is enforced here: a gateway carries an exact authority allowlist and an empty list denies everything.

requirements.summary: The key configuration used to generate encapsulated requests is integrity protected and authenticated so it can be attributed to the intended gateway.
requirements.reason: Attribution depends on the channel the configuration arrived over, which this package does not open. It refuses a configuration that is not exactly well formed and never substitutes a registry identifier it does not implement, so nothing it accepts is a silently altered one.

requirements.summary: Each sealed request draws a new ephemeral key from the platform entropy source, so no two requests share an HPKE context.
The request carrying an encapsulated request to the relay carries no identifying information the client cannot account for.
requirements.reason: What a client attaches to its own outbound request is chosen where that request is composed, and this package composes none. The value it produces for a relay to send is the gateway URI, the fixed content type, and the body, so nothing identifying comes from here.

requirements.summary: A relay forwarding a request follows the HTTP forwarding rules for intermediaries.
requirements.reason: The forwarding rules govern how an intermediary rewrites a live HTTP message, which needs the message and the connection it arrived on. This package models the relay as the fixed gateway identity plus the body to send, and holds no message to rewrite.

requirements.summary: A relay does not pass an unrecognised field through to the gateway.
Forwarding adds nothing that could identify a client beyond what the client already knows may be added.
Nothing a relay adds uniquely and permanently identifies a client, pseudonymous identifiers included.
Forwarding is a pure construction with no delay in it, so no client's latency is spent on timing mitigation without that client knowing.
A gateway is not usable as a relay to an arbitrary target: it carries an exact authority allowlist and an empty list denies every request.
A decapsulated request naming any scheme other than https is refused before it can reach a target.
The HPKE keys a gateway uses are bound to this protocol's own message/bhttp request label and are not valid for another protocol using the same label.
A failed request is not retried automatically unless something positively indicates it was neither processed nor forwarded.
requirements.reason: Retrying is a decision about a request in flight, and this package neither sends a request nor observes one failing. Every operation it exposes is a single pure transformation that either succeeds or returns a typed error to the caller that will make that decision.

requirements.summary: A client includes a Date field in encapsulated requests unless it knows the gateway does not use one for anti-replay.
requirements.reason: Which fields an encapsulated request carries is decided when the message is built, and the caller hands this codec a complete message to seal. The anti-replay this package does implement is an exact fingerprint set rather than a time window, so it needs no Date of its own.

requirements.summary: A gateway's anti-replay acceptance window is not treated as secret information.
requirements.reason: This gateway keeps no time window to treat as secret or otherwise. Its anti-replay is a finite fingerprint set that refuses an exact repeat and fails closed when it is full, so there is no interval whose value could be inferred or concealed.

requirements.summary: A retried request is a fresh encryption under a new HPKE context rather than a resend of the previous encapsulation.
A client adjusts the date and retries at most once.
requirements.reason: Counting retries belongs to whatever drives the exchange, and this package drives none: each seal is an independent call with no memory of an earlier one. It also implements no date-conditioned anti-replay for a client to be adjusting against.

requirements.summary: A gateway conditioning responses on the Date field keeps intermediaries from caching them, or varies on Date.
requirements.reason: Nothing here conditions a response on the Date field, so no response it produces is one this rule describes. Cache directives also live on the HTTP response the gateway composes, which this package does not build.

requirements.summary: The date a gateway reports is used for that one retry and for nothing else, including later requests to any resource.
requirements.reason: No value from a gateway response is retained anywhere in this package: opening a response yields the plaintext to the caller and keeps nothing. There is therefore no stored date for a later request to reuse.

requirements.summary: The hops that carry encapsulated messages use HTTPS, which the relay enforces on its gateway URI and the gateway enforces on the decapsulated target.

The accommodation provided against configuration tracking is that a collection is accepted whole or not at all and an unimplemented registry identifier is never substituted, so recovery behaviour does not vary between clients.

requirements.summary: Structured Field parsing is behaviorally equivalent to the RFC algorithms across every mandatory official vector.
The default bounded parser accepts Lists containing at least 1024 members.
The default bounded parser accepts Inner Lists containing at least 256 members.
Order-preserving Parameters have public bounded lookup operations by both wire index and key.
Canonical serialization omits the explicit value for a true Boolean Parameter while retaining false values.
The default parser accepts at least 256 Parameters and Parameter keys of at least 64 characters.
Order-preserving Dictionaries have public bounded lookup operations by both wire index and key.
Unknown Dictionary members remain syntactically accepted and do not prevent independent access to defined members.
Canonical serialization omits the explicit value of a Dictionary member whose Item value is Boolean true.
The default parser accepts at least 1024 Dictionary pairs and keys of at least 64 characters.
A String escape for any character other than DQUOTE or backslash fails the complete parse.
The default parser accepts decoded Strings containing at least 1024 characters.
The default parser accepts Tokens containing at least 512 characters.
The default parser accepts Byte Sequences containing at least 16384 octets after decoding.
Date parsing covers the complete RFC delta-second range spanning all days in years 1 through 9999.
Library-owned fields never choose Display String when String or Token is adequate; the generic codec preserves explicit caller choice only.
Byte Sequence serialization always emits canonical base64 whose unused pad bits are zero.
Matching field lines are combined once in wire order with comma and SP under an aggregate pre-allocation byte limit.
Any syntax or resource failure returns no partial value, selecting the RFC branch that invalidates the complete field value.
A recipient may alternatively reject the complete HTTP message when Structured Field parsing fails.
requirements.reason: The codec selects the RFC's other permitted branch by returning no partial field value; it does not own the enclosing HTTP message or force that optional alternative policy on callers.

requirements.summary: A parser is advised to accept an otherwise valid Byte Sequence whose terminal base64 padding is absent.
requirements.reason: The shared RFC 4648 contract requires padded canonical encodings so digest and signature inputs have one representation; the parser deliberately fails closed instead of synthesizing omitted padding.

requirements.summary: A parser is advised to accept base64 with nonzero unused pad bits when the decoder can be configured accordingly.
requirements.reason: The shared RFC 4648 contract rejects noncanonical pad bits to prevent alternate digest and signature representations of identical bytes; official advisory vectors record this fail-closed choice.

requirements.summary: Byte Sequence parsing rejects characters outside the base64 alphabet and every folded or bare line feed.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

entries.reason: The verified correction adds the accidentally omitted Display String to the enumerated Item kinds; the public data model and both codec directions explicitly include it.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: A match pattern outside the accepted URLPattern shape refuses the directive rather than being used against a request path.
A Use-As-Dictionary field without a match member carries no valid dictionary and is refused when it is parsed.
A dictionary whose match-dest list is empty is eligible for a request of any destination.
A client that does not support request destinations treats match-dest as an empty list and matches every destination.
requirements.reason: Selection here takes the request destination as a required argument, so the client this store serves does support destinations by construction. The fallback the requirement defines exists for a client that cannot supply one, and no caller of this API is in that position.

requirements.summary: A stored dictionary carrying a non-empty server identifier has that identifier sent as Dictionary-ID alongside Available-Dictionary.
requirements.reason: Which request fields are emitted is decided where the request is composed, and nothing in this package composes a dictionary-aware request. The store retains the identifier on the selected dictionary and serialize_dictionary_id produces the field from it, so the value and its serializer are supplied to the caller that does.

requirements.summary: The server identifier is carried and compared as an opaque string: nothing here reads structure out of it, only its length and text safety.
What a compressed body was built against is decided by the dictionary hash the stream carries, never by the identifier that accompanied it.
Expansion compares the stream's embedded thirty-two byte hash against the SHA-256 of the supplied dictionary and refuses a mismatch before decoding a byte.
A dictionary whose declared type is not raw is retained as an extension value and refused at insertion rather than used.
Selection returns exactly one dictionary, and the Available-Dictionary serializer carries the one hash belonging to it.
A dictionary whose freshness has passed the current time is not a match, so a stale entry is never selected.
Among matching dictionaries a destination-specific one wins, then the longest match, then the most recently fetched, in that order.
A request using a dictionary stored with a server-provided id carries that id in a Dictionary-ID request header.
requirements.reason: This is the same emission decision as the section 2.1.3 rule above and is made where the request is composed, which no module in this package does for dictionary transport. The identifier travels with the selected dictionary so the composer has it.

requirements.summary: Dictionary-ID is a Structured Fields String of at most 1024 characters after decoding, and it round trips identically to the identifier the server gave.
The default expansion ceiling admits a window log of 27, which is past the sixteen megabytes a dcb decoder has to accept.
The same window log of 27 is past both eight megabytes and 1.25 times the sixteen megabyte dictionary ceiling, which is the larger of the two a dcz decoder has to accept.
A stream whose encoded window exceeds the configured ceiling is refused during expansion rather than allocated for.
A request for which no stored dictionary matches, or for which the client declines one, does not advertise the dictionary-aware content codings.
requirements.reason: What a request advertises in Accept-Encoding is decided where the request is composed, and no module here composes one for dictionary transport. Selection reports NoMatchingDictionary rather than returning an unusable entry, which is the answer that decision needs.

requirements.summary: A cacheable dictionary-compressed response carries a Vary header so a cache cannot serve it to a client that did not ask for that encoding or that dictionary.
requirements.reason: Emitting Vary on a response is a decision for the origin that built it, and nothing in this package builds a dictionary-compressed response or serves one from a cache. This module encodes and decodes a body when a caller asks and adds no field of its own.

requirements.summary: A dictionary is stored and selected only against an https origin; any other scheme refuses the operation outright.
A stream whose magic, dictionary hash, window, or size ceiling does not hold produces a typed error rather than any output.
A client that hides response payloads from script and guards against cross-site tracking takes further steps so dictionary compression cannot leak across that boundary.
requirements.reason: The protection named is a user agent's: it depends on knowing which responses the page's script may read, which is a browser concept this package has no notion of. What it can partition, it does, by isolation key and by origin.

requirements.summary: In a user agent of that kind, dictionary compression is used only where both the dictionary and the compressed response are fully readable by the client.
requirements.reason: Readability in the sense the section means is a property of a browser's response taint model, and this package has no such model and serves no opaque response. The pairing it can enforce, that a body expands only against the dictionary its hash names, it enforces.

requirements.summary: Stored dictionaries are partitioned the way cookie state is: by top-level site and profile as well as by origin, so one partition cannot read or be probed through another.

standards.title: Security Considerations for Optimistic Protocol Transitions in HTTP/1.1

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: A CONNECT request with an empty, absent, non-numeric, or out-of-range target port is rejected before handler admission.
A WebSocket Upgrade client cannot send post-handshake data until a valid 101 response establishes the upgraded connection.
HTTP/1.x CONNECT-UDP datagrams remain unavailable until the 101 Upgrade response is validated.
The proxy client uses the strongest permitted mitigation: it sends only the CONNECT head and waits for a 2xx response before exposing a TCP payload channel.
A rejected HTTP/1.1 CONNECT always closes the underlying connection and discards pipelined bytes regardless of the request or response connection option.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: Every RateLimit-Policy list member has a Structured Fields String bare item.
A policy field should remain consistent across a sequence of responses.
requirements.reason: The codec serializes a supplied policy deterministically but deliberately owns no cross-response application policy store, so deployments must enforce semantic consistency at their policy source.

requirements.summary: Every quota policy item carries the required q parameter.
Implementation-specific policy parameters use a vendor-prefixed key.
RateLimit-Policy generation never permits a trailer section.
The q parameter is a non-negative Structured Fields Integer.
The qu parameter is represented only as a Structured Fields String.
A policy w parameter is a positive whole-second Integer.
A policy pk parameter is represented only as a Byte Sequence.
Every service limit item carries the required r parameter.
RateLimit generation never permits a trailer section.
Implementation-specific service-limit parameters use a vendor-prefixed key.
Positive remaining quota is exposed as a pacing hint rather than a service guarantee.
Client advice never assumes full quota restoration after an effective window.
A service-limit pk parameter is represented only as a Byte Sequence.
Retry-After does not end before the advertised effective window.
Generated fields cannot expose quota values above explicit finite application ceilings.
Generated quota-to-window ratios are bounded by an explicit units-per-second ceiling.
A service should document its deployment-specific partition-key generation algorithm.
requirements.reason: This is an application deployment and service-documentation obligation; a generic field codec has no partition algorithm or service documentation to publish.

requirements.summary: Servers should derive partition keys only from information present in the request.
requirements.reason: The codec preserves opaque partition-key bytes and cannot prove their application provenance; request-derived construction remains an explicitly documented server responsibility.

requirements.summary: Each response is interpreted independently without reusing a previous RateLimit field.
Malformed RateLimit fields produce IgnoreRateLimit instead of partial client advice.
Client advice provides bounded minimum request spacing over the effective window.
A valid Retry-After delay takes precedence over every RateLimit hint.
An intermediary replacement cannot make an upstream quota more permissive.
An intermediary should forward a request despite predicting quota rejection.
requirements.reason: The status field codec has no request-forwarding authority; it provides a restrictive mutation guard while the unified proxy policy must make the forwarding decision.

requirements.summary: RateLimit fields on responses with positive current age are ignored.
Available quota is exposed only as bounded advice and never as a service-level agreement.
